correctness.rationale: Rotation averaging follows from Rayleigh-quotient concavity of lambda_2, producing at least one alternating optimum. The Bloch lower band at theta=2pi/m gives lambda_2(a,b)=a+b-sqrt(g^2(a+b)^2+h(a-b)^2), including m=2. The stated unit-vector Cauchy-Schwarz inequality yields exact upper bound 2B sin^2(pi/m)/(m(p+q+2sqrt(pq)g)), attained by the explicit a*,b*>0. Equality is unique among alternating designs. For unrestricted independent edge weights, PSD equality under rotation averaging forces every vector of the repeated Fiedler eigenspace to be an eigenvector of each optimum. Subtraction at each B vertex gives a complex linear relation in two real edge deviations, with coefficients non-collinear because 1,r,e^(2pi i/m) are three distinct unit-circle points; both deviations must vanish. The m=2 two-dimensional Fiedler case separately forces all four equal. Direct independently computed m=3,p=1,q=4,B=1 yields a=2/21,b=5/84, gap 1/14 and matching full six-eigenvalue spectrum. No finite optimization is used as the uniqueness proof.
